clue.text: Parts of the capital that are in no way exceptional?

definitions.text: Parts of the capital that are in no way exceptional?

parts.words: Parts of the capital that are in no way exceptional?
parts.note: the capital is a company's share capital, and the parts of it that carry no special rights are described as plain and unremarkable

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which districts of the capital city are utterly unremarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests a city such as London, but it is a company's capital, divided into stock; the common stock with no preference is described here as 'in no way exceptional'.
explanation.definitionFit: Common stock in a company, carrying no preferential rights, is the standard holding that makes up most of its capital.

clue.text: Not a nudist who works behind the scenes at the sa theatre

definitions.text: who works behind the scenes at the sa theatre

explanation.surface: A theatre backstage worker is said to keep their clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts clothes on is the opposite of a nudist; in a theatre, the wardrobe assistant who helps actors change costumes has that title too.

clue.text: Bill's opponents

parts.note: a bill here is a draft law in Parliament, and its opponents are those who vote against it in a division

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name, but it is a parliamentary bill; those voting against it are counted as the negative votes.
explanation.definitionFit: Votes cast against a motion are the negatives in a parliamentary division, recorded as the lobby opposing it.

clue.text: Badly riled first mate coming in after someone else in has taken over duty?

definitions.text: after someone else in has taken over duty?

indicators.note: coming in tells us one piece enters the other and sits inside it
something done badly is messed up, so the letters of the word beside it are scrambled

parts.note: Eve was the first wife, Adam's mate, in the Bible

explanation.surface: A ship's first mate, in a bad temper, arrives just after a colleague has taken over the watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' puts EVE inside RELID (the anagram of RILED, from 'Badly'), between RELI and D. 'First mate' suggests a ship's officer; it is Eve, the first wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard or worker is freed from duty when a replacement arrives to take over the post.

clue.text: A melody the artist isn't ti worried about

indicators.note: worried about suggests letters fussed over and pushed around, so they are rearranged

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the standard crossword artist
the letters of this word, its apostrophe dropped, are used as they stand

explanation.surface: A painter is unconcerned about a certain tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried about' rearranges RA plus ISNT into a six-letter word for a tune. RA, a member of the Royal Academy, is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a passage of music or a tune, as in 'the strains of a waltz'.

clue.text: They are trained to come up with constructive ideas

definitions.text: They are trained to come up with constructive ideas

parts.words: They are trained to come up with constructive ideas
parts.note: constructive is read literally: the ideas are for buildings, and these professionals are trained to design them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Constructive ideas' sounds like helpful suggestions, but the ideas are literally for construction: designs for buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: Building designers are professionals trained to draw up plans for structures.

clue.text: One impression of literary Op work

definitions.text: One impression of literary Op work

parts.words: One impression of literary Op work
parts.note: an impression is a single print run of a book, so one issue of a published work; 'Op' is print debris

explanation.walkthrough: 'Impression' suggests an opinion of a book, but in publishing it is one print run of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A published version of a book issued at one time is a single print run or issue.

clue.text: Favourite places for train thing?

parts.note: the places most wanted in a railway carriage are the ones against the window at the end of a row

explanation.walkthrough: Many travellers make for the seats in the angle of a railway compartment, by the window.
explanation.definitionFit: Seats in the angle of a compartment, beside the window, are the most sought after on a train.

clue.text: Dealer in valuable articles we'll make gibes about

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: to make gibes is to jeer
the letters of we'll, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: We promise to mock a trader in valuables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts JEER round WELL: JE + WELL + ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader in gems, rings and other precious items is the shopkeeper who sells fine adornments.

clue.text: A capital atmosphere in a small business organisation

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation (small) of company, a business organisation
air is the atmosphere around us

explanation.surface: A city's business climate is described within a small firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts AIR inside CO. 'small' tells us the business organisation is shortened to its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Egypt's chief city is a national seat of government.

clue.text: Political subterfuges at M which conjurers should be adept

definitions.text: Political subterfuges at M which conjurers should be adept

parts.words: Political subterfuges at M which conjurers should be adept
parts.note: the ruses of a political faction share their name with the sleight-of-hand turns an entertainer does at a social gathering

explanation.walkthrough: 'Political' points to a political faction's schemes, but the same phrase names the little tricks a magician performs at a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Conjuring tricks done to entertain guests at a social gathering go by this name, and it reads also as a political faction's ruses.

clue.text: Further out of Laos

indicators.note: out of here means put out of order, so the letters of the country are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone travels further out of the Asian country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Further' looks like a direction, but it is the definition meaning 'in addition'; 'out of' rearranges LAOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Further in the sense 'moreover' or 'in addition' is a synonym.

clue.text: It explains precisely what is meant by sharpness of outline

definitions.text: It explains precisely what is meant

explanation.surface: Something clarifies meaning through a crisp outline.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary entry explains a word's exact meaning, and in photography or television the crispness of an image's edges has the same name.

clue.text: What the sentry said to the ta Quaker with satisfactory to credentials?

parts.note: a pass is a satisfactory grade in an exam
Quakers belong to the Religious Society of Friends, so a Quaker is a Friend

explanation.surface: A sentry lets through a Quaker whose papers are in order.
explanation.walkthrough: A sentry challenges with 'Who goes there?' and lets an ally through with these words. 'With' only joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The sentry's words letting through someone identified as an ally are the traditional permission to proceed.

clue.text: Where football hooligans can create havoc with Southern Region

indicators.note: to create havoc is to wreck things, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: SR is the abbreviation for Southern Region, the old British Rail region

explanation.surface: Football thugs are able to cause chaos on the Southern Region trains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'havoc' rearranges CREATE with SR into the stepped stands of a football ground. Southern Region was a division of British Rail serving the south of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Stepped standing areas at British football grounds were where the rowdiest supporters gathered.

clue.text: Far too much to pay for apple turnover!

indicators.note: a turnover turns the word upside down, so the apple's name is read backwards

parts.note: a rennet (reinette) is a variety of dessert apple

explanation.surface: Ten pounds is an outrageous price for a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apple turnover' looks like the pastry, but 'turnover' reverses RENNET, a kind of apple. A ten-pound note was a lot to pay for a pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-pound note, in British slang, would be an outrageous price for a small pastry.

clue.text: Back on the field of play, maybe

definitions.text: Back on the field of play, maybe

parts.words: Back on the field of play, maybe
parts.note: a back in football or hockey is a player whose job is guarding the goal area

explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reads as 'returning', but a back is a team position whose task is to stop attacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A back in football is a player stationed near the goal to stop attackers, a guarding role.

clue.text: Throaty complaint of young and beautiful singer?

explanation.surface: A gifted young singer suffers a sore throat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fungal infection of the mouth common in babies shares its name with a songbird famed for its music.

clue.text: Put into a new bed at the nursery?

definitions.text: Put into a new bed at the nursery?

parts.words: Put into a new bed at the nursery?
parts.note: nursery reads as a children's room, but it is a garden nursery and the bed is a flower bed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nursery' and 'bed' suggest a child moved to a new cot; it is a plant nursery moving seedlings to another flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving a plant from one patch of soil to another and setting it in the ground again is the gardener's task.

clue.text: Grasping member of the animal kingdom

definitions.text: Grasping member of the animal kingdom

parts.words: Grasping member of the animal kingdom
parts.note: member reads as a person in a group, but it is a limb, one used for gripping by an octopus or squid

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grasping member' sounds like a greedy person in a club; it is a limb that grips, as on an octopus.
explanation.definitionFit: The long flexible arm an octopus or squid uses to seize prey is a gripping limb.

clue.text: Small wheaten loaf for smokers?

parts.note: a cob is a small round loaf and corn is grain, but smokers use a pipe made from a maize husk core

explanation.walkthrough: A cob is a small round loaf in Britain and corn is grain, so the phrase sounds like bread; smokers know it as a cheap pipe carved from the core of a maize ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A tobacco pipe with a bowl made from the core of an ear of maize is a smoker's item.

clue.text: Defer a decision to leave the shore

explanation.surface: Someone delays deciding whether to set sail.
explanation.definitionFit: To postpone something is to delay it; a boat setting out from land is said to push out to sea in the same words.

clue.text: One trump I'd vexatiously pressed for

indicators.note: vexatiously suggests something stirred up and agitated, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A card player annoyingly demands a trump card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vexatiously' rearranges ONETRUMPID, ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To pester someone persistently with demands is to beg or press them for something.

clue.text: Extremist who wants the Labour party to move briskly forward

definitions.text: Extremist who wants the Labour party

explanation.surface: A left-wing militant wants the Labour party to hurry up.
explanation.walkthrough: A Trotskyist was nicknamed a Trot, and some tried to steer Britain's Labour Party leftward.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trotskyist militant is known by this short form, and a horse's brisk gait between walk and canter has the same name.

clue.text: What we put on the plate when in church?

definitions.text: What we put on the plate when in church?

parts.words: What we put on the plate when in church?
parts.note: plate reads as a dinner plate, but it is the collection plate passed round in a church service for money

explanation.walkthrough: 'Plate' suggests food, but in church it is the collection plate where worshippers leave money.
explanation.definitionFit: Coins and notes are what churchgoers place on the collection plate as an offering.

clue.text: Jack in a deal, maybe

parts.note: Jack reads as a man's name, but it is the playing card, which turns up in a deal of cards

explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a man and 'deal' a bargain, but the jack is a court card found in a deal of cards, also called by an old word for a rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: In a pack of playing cards the jack is also known by an old name for a rascal.

clue.text: Kind of survey maps the Artillery cannot do without

explanation.surface: Gunners rely on official maps of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ordnance Survey is Britain's national mapping agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's official map series is named for military supplies, which are the big guns and munitions gunners depend on.

clue.text: Prepare to take silk or become a licensed victualler?

explanation.surface: A choice between a legal career and running a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: To take silk is to become a senior barrister in Britain; a licensed victualler is a pub landlord, who works behind the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Law students preparing to become barristers read for entry to the legal profession; a would-be publican trains to serve drinks at a pub counter.
